resources.string: While the tunnel to the NAS runs, with “Disconnect”.
The tunnel should run but could not start by itself.
Android has not allowed the VPN for TitanOS yet. Tap “Connect” in the app and confirm.
The internet address of the NAS could not be resolved. Is there internet? Is the name under Settings › WireGuard right?
The tunnel could not start. Please try again; if that does not help, make the access anew.
Android stopped the start in the background. Tap to connect. With the exception from battery optimisation it works by itself in future.
The key of this phone cannot be read any more. Please make the access anew.
The phone has no network right now.
In a home Wi-Fi: the tunnel is not needed.
Not set up yet: create the access below.
Away: the tunnel should be on but is not.
Switched by hand, until the network changes.
Another VPN runs, such as Tailscale. Automatic does not replace it.
Android’s always-on VPN is on: the tunnel always stays on.
No contact with the NAS yet
In the mode “Never” the tunnel does not come on. Change it under “When” below.

The app adds a WireGuard access of its own for this phone on the NAS. The key is made here and stays on the phone; the NAS gets only the public part. The access then shows on the NAS under Settings › WireGuard.

The WireGuard server of the NAS is off. In the browser, switch it on under Settings › Network and remote access › WireGuard, enter the address from the internet and forward UDP 51820 to the NAS on the router.
WireGuard on the NAS has no address from the internet. Enter it under Settings › WireGuard or set up dynamic DNS.
Only owners and administrators may create a WireGuard access. This account has no administration rights.
Another device has this key already. Please try again.
The NAS has 50 WireGuard devices already. Please remove one there.
The NAS cannot be reached right now.
The NAS keeps this access out of the tunnel right now: the account is locked or has no administration rights.
The access was removed on the NAS. Create it here again when it is needed.
The phone makes a new key; the old one stops working on the NAS at once. The address in the tunnel stays.
The tunnel closes, the key is deleted on the phone and the device disappears on the NAS under Settings › WireGuard.
On outside the home Wi-Fi networks, off at home.
With the button here, the tile or the notification.
The tunnel stays off; the tile does not switch it on either.
At home the tunnel stays off in the mode Automatic. The app remembers Wi-Fi networks in which the NAS answers directly.
When the NAS answers directly in a Wi-Fi, it goes on the list.
Android tells the name of the Wi-Fi only to apps with location permission. The app uses it only for this, never for the place, and sends none of it to the NAS.
So that the tunnel comes on by itself when you leave the Wi-Fi while the app is closed: choose “Allow all the time” for location in Android.
Location is switched off on the phone. Without it Android names no Wi-Fi.
Default. Only connections to the NAS go through the tunnel, everything else as usual.
Also the router, printers and other devices at home. Can get in the way in another Wi-Fi with the same address range.
The whole internet goes through the NAS at home. IPv6 does not work then.
Every app reaches the NAS through the tunnel, the browser too.
Other apps go past the tunnel.
The DNS servers from Settings › WireGuard on the NAS: %1$s
No DNS server is entered on the NAS under Settings › WireGuard.
A small packet every few seconds so routers do not forget the tunnel.
Connect in the mode Automatic even while another VPN runs. Android allows only one VPN.
Android then always keeps the tunnel on and can block connections without VPN. Set it in Android under Network › VPN › TitanOS. The setting “When” does not apply then.
Still missing: Android asks once at the first connection.
Active: Android then cannot always start the tunnel by itself in the background.
The notification shows while the tunnel runs and offers “Disconnect”.
Switches the tunnel in Quick Settings. In the mode Automatic it holds until the network changes.
Tailscale stays possible, but Android allows only one VPN at a time.
Tunnel to the NAS when away
